created_roles.name: Scheduling Analyst
created_roles.description: Operations-research minded engineer who solves small scheduling problems exactly. Enumerates every assignment so that optimality is proved rather than argued.
created_roles.prompt: You are a senior scheduling analyst. Problem: jobs of 4, 7 and 9 hours; two identical machines run in parallel; each job runs on exactly one machine; minimise makespan = max machine load. Method: (1) With Bash/python3 (itertools.product over machine labels 1,2 for the three jobs) enumerate all 8 assignments; for each compute load M1, load M2 and makespan, and assert that each job appears on exactly one machine and that the loads sum to 20. If Bash is unavailable, compute by hand and confirm each sum with calc. (2) Print a markdown table with columns: #, Machine 1 jobs, Machine 2 jobs, Load M1, Load M2, Makespan (8 rows). (3) Below the table give a bullet list: the minimum makespan; the optimal assignment(s), noting that swapping machine labels gives the mirror assignment; the number of distinct assignments up to symmetry (4); the lower bound max(9, ceil(20/2)=10)=10, noting that the optimum does not meet it because no subset of {4,7,9} sums to 10; and the confirmation that every job runs on exactly one machine in every row.
created_roles.goal: Produce the full enumeration of all 8 assignments with loads and makespans, and identify the minimum and the optimal assignment.
responsibilities: Restate the problem: two machines run in parallel, each job runs on exactly one machine, makespan definition
Enumerate all 2^3 assignments with machine loads and makespan
Check per row that each job appears exactly once and loads sum to 20
Identify the minimum, the optimal assignment(s) and the symmetry
State the lower bound max(longest job, ceil(total/2)) and compare it to the optimum
inputs: Task statement: jobs 4, 7, 9 and two parallel machines

outputs.format: markdown table: assignment id x jobs on Machine 1 x jobs on Machine 2 x load M1 x load M2 x makespan, plus a list stating the minimum, optimal assignment and lower bound

success_criteria: Exactly 8 rows, each job on exactly one machine in every row
Loads in each row sum to 20
Minimum makespan and optimal assignment clearly identified
constraints: Two machines only, running in parallel
Do not skip assignments, including the one with all jobs on a single machine

created_roles.name: Independent Verifier
created_roles.description: Reviewer who re-derives results without looking at the original working, so errors are caught by independence. Checks completeness and arithmetic.
created_roles.prompt: You are a senior verifier. First, without looking at the analyst's numbers, list all subsets of {4,7,9} as Machine 1's jobs (8 subsets); the rest run on Machine 2, so each job runs on exactly one of the two parallel machines. Compute both loads and the makespan for each (use calc or python3 via Bash). Then compare with the analyst's table row by row, marking each match or mismatch. Check: 8 rows, every job exactly once per row, loads sum to 20, the minimum, the optimal assignment, the symmetry statement, and that the lower-bound claim is right (no subset sums to 10, so 11 is optimal). Output a memo with headings: Independent recomputation (table), Comparison, Verdict. The verdict line must say VERDICT: PASS or VERDICT: FAIL, with corrections if any.
created_roles.goal: Confirm or refute the enumeration and the claimed optimum.
responsibilities: Independently enumerate the subsets of jobs for Machine 1 and recompute loads and makespans
Compare against the analyst's table row by row
Check completeness (8 rows), each job on exactly one machine, loads summing to 20, the minimum and the lower-bound argument
Issue a verdict with any corrections
inputs: Enumeration table and conclusions from step 1

outputs.format: memo: independent recomputation table, row-by-row match list, verdict (PASS/FAIL) with corrections

success_criteria: Every row matched or corrected
Verdict explicitly stated
Minimum and optimal assignment independently confirmed
constraints: Recompute from the task numbers, not by copying the analyst's figures

created_roles.name: Final Report Writer
created_roles.description: Technical writer who assembles the verified results into a short, clear answer without adding new analysis.
created_roles.prompt: Assemble the final answer from the verified material only. Structure: Answer (minimum makespan and the optimal assignment with each machine's jobs and load, noting the mirror by swapping machines); Optimality check (the table of all 8 assignments with makespans, one sentence that the smallest value is the optimum, plus the lower-bound remark, and a note that in every row each job runs on exactly one of the two parallel machines); Assumptions (identical machines running in parallel, no splitting, all jobs available at time 0); Verification (one line giving the verifier's verdict). If the verifier reported corrections, use the corrected figures. Do not add analysis of your own.
created_roles.goal: Deliver the final answer: makespan, assignment and the all-assignments optimality table.
responsibilities: Assemble the final answer from the verified outputs
Use the verifier's corrections if any
Keep it concise and consistent

outputs.format: memo: answer (makespan, assignment), table of all 8 assignments, optimality statement

success_criteria: States makespan 11 and the assignment (if verified)
Includes all 8 assignments
Notes assumptions and the verification verdict
constraints: No new analysis; use only the verified figures

## Requirements:
R1: Model the two machines as running in parallel, and make each of the three jobs (4, 7, 9 hours) run on exactly one machine.
R2: Find the assignment of the jobs to the two machines that minimises the makespan (the time the last machine finishes).
R3: Give the minimum makespan value.
R4: Give the optimal assignment explicitly (which jobs run on which machine, with each machine's load).
R5: Show optimality by checking every assignment (all 2^3 = 8 labelled assignments, with the machine-swap symmetry noted), giving each one's makespan.
R6: Check that in every enumerated assignment each job runs on exactly one machine and that the two parallel machines' loads sum to 20 hours.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Job durations: 4, 7, 9 hours; total work = 4 + 7 + 9 = 20 hours.
- Two identical machines run in parallel; each job runs wholly on exactly one machine (no splitting, no preemption).
- Makespan = max(load of machine 1, load of machine 2).
- Number of assignments = 2^3 = 8 labelled (4 distinct up to swapping machines).
- Lower bounds: ceil(20/2) = 10 and longest job = 9, so makespan >= 10.
- Expected enumeration: {}|{4,7,9} = 20 (x2 with swap); {4}|{7,9} = max(4,16) = 16 (x2); {7}|{4,9} = max(7,13) = 13 (x2); {9}|{4,7} = max(9,11) = 11 (x2). Minimum = 11. This hand calculation is to be confirmed by the steps.
- Assumption: machines are identical (same speed), with no setup times, release dates or precedence constraints; all jobs are available at time 0.
- Assumption: the case with all jobs on one machine (the other idle) is allowed and is included in the enumeration.

## Open Questions:
- question: Are the two machines identical in speed and are job times independent of the machine? | assumption: Yes, identical machines; the hours given apply on either machine.
- question: Is the optimal assignment unique? | assumption: It is unique up to relabelling the machines; the deliverable names one labelling (Machine A: 9; Machine B: 4+7) and notes the swap.

rounds.planner_raw:
## Requirements:
R1: Model the two machines as running in parallel, and make each of the three jobs (4, 7, 9 hours) run on exactly one machine.
R2: Find the assignment of the jobs to the two machines that minimises the makespan (the time the last machine finishes).
R3: Give the minimum makespan value.
R4: Give the optimal assignment explicitly (which jobs run on which machine, with each machine's load).
R5: Show optimality by checking every assignment (all 2^3 = 8 labelled assignments, with the machine-swap symmetry noted), giving each one's makespan.
R6: Check that in every enumerated assignment each job runs on exactly one machine and that the two parallel machines' loads sum to 20 hours.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- Job durations: 4, 7, 9 hours; total work = 4 + 7 + 9 = 20 hours.
- Two identical machines run in parallel; each job runs wholly on exactly one machine (no splitting, no preemption).
- Makespan = max(load of machine 1, load of machine 2).
- Number of assignments = 2^3 = 8 labelled (4 distinct up to swapping machines).
- Lower bounds: ceil(20/2) = 10 and longest job = 9, so makespan >= 10.
- Expected enumeration: {}|{4,7,9} = 20 (x2 with swap); {4}|{7,9} = max(4,16) = 16 (x2); {7}|{4,9} = max(7,13) = 13 (x2); {9}|{4,7} = max(9,11) = 11 (x2). Minimum = 11. This hand calculation is to be confirmed by the steps.
- Assumption: machines are identical (same speed), with no setup times, release dates or precedence constraints; all jobs are available at time 0.
- Assumption: the case with all jobs on one machine (the other idle) is allowed and is included in the enumeration.

## Open Questions:
- question: Are the two machines identical in speed and are job times independent of the machine? | assumption: Yes, identical machines; the hours given apply on either machine.
- question: Is the optimal assignment unique? | assumption: It is unique up to relabelling the machines; the deliverable names one labelling (Machine A: 9; Machine B: 4+7) and notes the swap.

requirements.R1: Model the two machines as running in parallel, and make each of the three jobs (4, 7, 9 hours) run on exactly one machine.
requirements.R2: Find the assignment of the jobs to the two machines that minimises the makespan (the time the last machine finishes).
requirements.R4: Give the optimal assignment explicitly (which jobs run on which machine, with each machine's load).
requirements.R5: Show optimality by checking every assignment (all 2^3 = 8 labelled assignments, with the machine-swap symmetry noted), giving each one's makespan.

givens: Job durations: 4, 7, 9 hours; total work = 4 + 7 + 9 = 20 hours.
Two identical machines run in parallel; each job runs wholly on exactly one machine (no splitting, no preemption).
Makespan = max(load of machine 1, load of machine 2).
Number of assignments = 2^3 = 8 labelled (4 distinct up to swapping machines).
Lower bounds: ceil(20/2) = 10 and longest job = 9, so makespan >= 10.

Expected enumeration: {}|{4,7,9} = 20 (x2 with swap); {4}|{7,9} = max(4,16) = 16 (x2); {7}|{4,9} = max(7,13) = 13 (x2); {9}|{4,7} = max(9,11) = 11 (x2). Minimum = 11. This hand calculation is to be confirmed by the steps.
Assumption: machines are identical (same speed), with no setup times, release dates or precedence constraints; all jobs are available at time 0.
Assumption: the case with all jobs on one machine (the other idle) is allowed and is included in the enumeration.
risks: Mislabelled or missed assignment (e.g. forgetting the all-on-one-machine case): mitigated by the independent verifier and the 8-row check.
Bash/python unavailable: fall back to hand arithmetic confirmed with calc; the problem is small enough.
Ambiguity about machine speeds or constraints: settled by the identical-machines assumption, stated in the final answer.
Decision point: if the verifier returns FAIL, rerun step 1 with the corrections before step 3.
